questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Poona pact and choose the correct option.

**Statement (I):** This pact was made between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. Ambedkar in 1932.

**Statement (II):** Under this pact, seats are reserved in provincial and central legislative councils for the Depressed Classes
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Both Statement (I) and Statement (II)**** are true**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__*** **Here's a detailed explanation of each statement:*

**Statement (I): This pact was made between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. Ambedkar in 1932.**

 
• This statement is **true**.
 
• The Poona Pact was an agreement signed between Mahatma Gandhi, the leader of the Indian National Congress, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the leader of the Scheduled Castes Federation, on September 24, 1932.
 
• The pact was signed after a series of negotiations between the two leaders in Pune, India.

**Statement (II): Under this pact, seats are reserved in provincial and central legislative councils for the Depressed Classes**

 
• Ambedkar ultimately agreed to Gandhiji’s stance, leading to the Poona Pact of September 1932. This pact provided reserved seats for the Depressed Classes (later known as the Scheduled Castes) in the provincial and central legislative councils, with the stipulation that these representatives would be elected by the general electorate
 
• To provide some context, the British Government had introduced the Communal Award in 1932, which provided for separate electorates for the Depressed Classes in British India.
 
• This move was welcomed by Ambedkar and other Dalit leaders, who saw it as a way to ensure that the interests of the Depressed Classes were adequately represented in the legislative councils.
 
• However, Gandhi was vehemently opposed to the idea of separate electorates.
 
• He believed that they would only serve to perpetuate the caste system and create further divisions between different communities in India.
 
• As a result, Gandhi went on a fast-unto-death to protest against the Communal Award.
 
• After negotiations between Gandhi and Ambedkar, the Poona Pact was signed.
 
• While it did not provide for separate electorates, it did include provisions for reserved seats for the Depressed Classes in the legislative councils.
 
• These seats would be elected by joint electorates, meaning that all voters, regardless of their caste, would have the right to vote for candidates from the Depressed Classes.
 
• So, **while Statement (II) is not entirely accurate, it does contain an element of truth in that the issue of separate electorates was a major factor in the negotiations that led to the signing of the Poona Pact**.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Vedanta philosophy:

1. Shankara was the founder of Advaita Vedanta.

2. The philosophy of Dvaita was elaborated by Madhva.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is *__** Both 1 and 2.**__*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Vedanta Philosophy**

__
 
• **Shankara** was indeed the founder of **Advaita Vedanta**, a non-dualistic school of Hindu philosophy.

 
 
• Advaita Vedanta emphasizes the idea that the **individual self (Atman)** and the **universal self (Brahman)** are one and the same.
 
• Shankara, also known as **Adi Shankaracharya**, lived in the **8th century** and was a prominent philosopher and theologian.
 
• He wrote extensive commentaries on the **Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita**, and **Brahma Sutras** to propagate his philosophy.
 
 
 
• Hence, **statement 1 is correct**.
 
• The philosophy of **Dvaita** was elaborated by **Madhva**.
 
 
• Madhva, also known as **Madhvacharya**, founded the **dualistic (Dvaita) school** of Vedanta in the **13th century**.
 
• According to Dvaita, the **individual soul (Atman)** and the **supreme soul (Brahman)** are distinct and separate entities.
 
• Madhva's teachings were primarily focused on the worship of **Vishnu** as the supreme deity.
 
 
 
• Hence, **statement 2 is correct**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Advaita Vedanta**:

 
 
• Advaita Vedanta is one of the most influential schools of Hindu philosophy.
 
• Its primary tenet is that there is no distinction between the **individual self (Atman)** and the **universal self (Brahman)**.
 
• Shankara's works include **commentaries** on major Hindu scriptures and numerous other philosophical texts.
 
 
 
• **Dvaita Vedanta**:
 
 
• Dvaita Vedanta, or dualistic Vedanta, asserts that God (Vishnu) and individual souls are eternally distinct.
 
• Madhvacharya, the proponent of this philosophy, argued against the non-dualistic teachings of Shankara.
 
• His works include commentaries on the **Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita**, and **Brahma Sutras**, as well as independent treatises.

questions.question:
Work done on an object depends upon which of the following factors?

1. Displacement

2. Angle between force and displacement

​3. Initial speed of the object

4. Force applied
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2 and 4 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Work done** depends on the displacement of the object, as it represents the distance moved under the influence of force.
 
• The **angle between force and displacement** determines the effective component of the force contributing to the work.
 
• The magnitude of the **force applied** directly impacts the work done, as work is calculated as the product of force, displacement, and the cosine of the angle.
 
• Initial speed of the object does **not influence work done** directly; work depends on the change in kinetic energy or force-displacement dynamics.
 
• Work is mathematically expressed as **W = F . d × cos(θ)**, where F is force, d is displacement, and θ is the angle between force and displacement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work:** Work is defined as the transfer of energy when a force is applied to an object causing displacement.
 
• **Force:** It refers to an interaction that changes the motion of an object, impacting the calculation of work.
 
• **Displacement:** This is the vector quantity describing the change in position of an object, essential for evaluating work.
 
• **Cosine of the angle:** The angle θ between the force and displacement affects the effective force contributing to the work, with cos(θ) ranging from -1 to +1.
 
• **Energy transfer:** Work done on an object is directly related to the change in its energy, such as kinetic or potential energy.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements correctly explains the cause of volcanism?

options.text: It results from molten rock rising from the Earth’s interior.
It is caused by excessive surface erosion.
It happens because of atmospheric disturbances.
It is due to the movement of glaciers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It results from molten rock rising from the Earth's interior.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Volcanism occurs when molten rock, known as magma, rises from the Earth's mantle to the surface, driven by pressure differences and tectonic activity.
 
• At tectonic plate boundaries, such as divergent and convergent zones, magma can escape and form volcanic eruptions.
 
• The molten rock that reaches the surface is called lava, and it solidifies to create various landforms like volcanoes, lava domes, and plateaus.
 
• Volcanism is often associated with hotspots, where mantle plumes push magma to the surface, as seen in regions like Hawaii and Yellowstone.
 
• Volcanic eruptions contribute to the Earth's geological processes, including the formation of new crust, landforms, and mineral deposits.

__
 
• The Gupta period (approximately 320–550 CE) is often referred to as the **Golden Age of India** due to its remarkable contributions to art, literature, science, and culture.
 
• During this era, India witnessed significant advancements in **mathematics, astronomy, medicine, and philosophy**. Aryabhata and Varahamihira were prominent scholars of this period.
 
• The Gupta Empire is renowned for its contributions to **literature and Sanskrit poetry**, with Kalidasa being the most famous poet and playwright.
 
• Architectural and artistic achievements thrived, including the construction of temples and the development of intricate sculptures and paintings, such as the Ajanta caves.
 
• This period also saw the promotion of Hinduism, along with the flourishing of Buddhism and Jainism, creating a rich and diverse cultural landscape.

• The Renaissance refers to the cultural movement that occurred in Europe between the 14th and 17th centuries, marked by a renewed interest in classical learning and the arts.
 
• It began in Italy and focused on humanism, scientific inquiry, and artistic expression, with notable figures like Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Galileo.
 
• This term is not used to describe any period in Indian history, as it specifically relates to a European historical phenomenon.
 
 
 
• **The Age of Enlightenment**
 
 
• The Enlightenment, also known as the Age of Reason, was a European intellectual and philosophical movement during the 17th and 18th centuries.
 
• It emphasized reason, individualism, and skepticism of traditional doctrines, influencing revolutions like the American and French Revolutions.
 
• This term does not apply to the Gupta period in India, as it is a specific Western historical development.
 
 
 
• **The Age of Revolutions**
 
 
• The Age of Revolutions refers to the period from the late 18th to the mid-19th centuries, marked by significant political and social upheavals worldwide.
 
• Notable events include the American Revolution, the French Revolution, and the Industrial Revolution.
 
• This term does not align with the Gupta period, as the Gupta era was characterized by stability, prosperity, and cultural advancements rather than revolutions.

Consider the following statements:

**Statement I:** DPSPs are subordinate to Fundamental Rights in all situations.

**Statement II:** Certain DPSPs have been given primacy over Fundamental Rights through constitutional amendments.

Which one of the following is correct?

options.text: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option D**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The statement that **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) are subordinate to Fundamental Rights in all situations** is **not correct**. While DPSPs are generally non-justiciable, the Constitution has evolved through amendments and judicial interpretation to alter this relationship. Hence, **Statement I is incorrect**.
 
• Certain DPSPs have been accorded **primacy over Fundamental Rights** through **constitutional amendments**, most notably **Article 31C**, which gives precedence to laws enacted to implement **Article 39(b) and 39(c)** over Articles 14 and 19. Hence, **Statement II is correct**.
 
• Thus, **Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct → Option D**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 31C** was introduced by the **25th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971** and later expanded by the **42nd Amendment**, though the expansion was curtailed by the Supreme Court.
 
• In **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)**, the Supreme Court upheld Article 31C **only to the extent of Articles 39(b) and (c)**.
 
• The Court has consistently held that **Fundamental Rights and DPSPs are complementary**, not antagonistic (e.g., **Minerva Mills case, 1980**).
 
• The current constitutional position seeks a **harmonious balance** between individual liberties and socio-economic justice.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding connective tissue?

options.text: Fat storing adipose tissue is found above the skin
Areolar connective tissue is found between the skin and muscle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fat storing adipose tissue is found above the skin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Adipose tissue**, commonly referred to as fat tissue, is primarily located beneath the skin (subcutaneous layer), around internal organs, and in certain areas of the body like the abdomen and thighs.
 
• It serves as **energy storage**, insulation to maintain body temperature, and cushioning to protect vital organs.
 
• The statement that fat-storing adipose tissue is found above the skin is incorrect, as adipose tissue is specifically located **beneath the skin** (subcutaneous layer) rather than above it.
 
• Adipose tissue is classified into two types: **white adipose tissue (WAT)**, which stores energy and insulates the body, and **brown adipose tissue (BAT)**, which generates heat through thermogenesis.
 
• The primary function of adipose tissue is to store triglycerides and release them when the body requires energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ligaments connect bone to bone:**
 
 
• Ligaments are tough, fibrous connective tissues that connect bones to other bones, providing stability to joints.
 
• They are primarily made of collagen fibers, giving them strength and flexibility.
 
• Ligaments prevent excessive movement and dislocation of joints, ensuring proper alignment during physical activity.
 
• Examples include the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in the knee and the ulnar collateral ligament in the elbow.
 
 
 
• **Areolar connective tissue is found between the skin and muscle:**
 
 
• Areolar connective tissue is a loose connective tissue that fills the space between organs and connects the skin to underlying muscles.
 
• It contains fibroblasts, collagen, and elastic fibers, allowing flexibility and support.
 
• Areolar tissue plays a significant role in providing a medium for nutrient and waste exchange between blood vessels and cells.
 
• It also houses immune cells that help defend the body against pathogens in the surrounding tissues.
 
 
 
• **Tendons connect muscle to bone:**
 
 
• Tendons are strong, fibrous connective tissues that attach muscles to bones, enabling movement of the skeleton.
 
• They are composed of dense regular connective tissue with parallel collagen fibers, allowing them to withstand tension during muscle contraction.
 
• Examples include the Achilles tendon, which connects the calf muscles to the heel bone.
 
• Tendons work in coordination with muscles to ensure efficient movement and force transmission during physical activities.

__
 
• **Statement A:** Black soil covers most of the **Deccan Plateau**, specifically in states like **Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh**. It is highly fertile and suitable for the cultivation of crops like cotton. *This statement is correct.*
 
• **Statement B:** Black soil is indeed rich in **lime, iron, magnesium, and alumina**. However, it does not lack magnesium; rather, it lacks phosphorus, nitrogen, and organic matter. This makes the statement factually incorrect. 
 
• Since Statement B is incorrect, the option stating that Statement A is accurate.
 
• *Black soil is also known as **Regur soil** or **cotton soil**, and it has a fine texture and retains moisture well, which is ideal for dry farming.*
 
• **Hence, Option 2 is the correct answer, because statement (b) is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Black Soil Characteristics:**

 
 
• Black soil is formed from **lava basalt rocks**, making it one of the most fertile soils in India.
 
• It is highly suitable for crops like **cotton, sugarcane, tobacco, oilseeds, and pulses**.
 
• Its fine-grained structure allows it to retain moisture, but it becomes extremely hard when dry.
 
• It is rich in **lime, iron, magnesium, and alumina**, but lacks **nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic matter**.

• It is predominantly found in the **Deccan Plateau** regions such as **Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh.**
 
 
 
• **Uses of Black Soil:**
 
 
• Black soil is primarily used for cultivating **cotton**, which is why it is also known as **cotton soil**.
 
• Due to its moisture-retaining ability, it is ideal for crops requiring less irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Black soil is classified as one of the **seven soil types in India**, along with Alluvial, Red, Laterite, Desert, Mountain, and Peaty soils.
 
• The soil is highly fertile but requires supplementation of **nitrogen and phosphorus fertilizers** to support crop growth efficiently.
 
• It is an essential resource for agricultural productivity in India.

• They acted as intermediaries between the British government and the princely states.

questions.question: If cot x = (4)/(3) then find the value of (sin x - cos x)/(sin x + cos x)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given cot x = 4/3. We know that cot x = cos x / sin x.

Since the given expression is homogeneous in terms of sin x and cos x, we can directly substitute cos x = 4 and sin x = 3.

Expression = (sin x − cos x) / (sin x + cos x)

⇒ Expression = (3 − 4) / (3 + 4)

⇒ Expression = −1 / 7

**∴ The correct answer is −1/7.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cot x = 4/3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/306701f87c0d708b2357000c73b09ed1b67c794c32dce9ec8e45b3509ff54d78.png] 

**Formula Used:**

cot x = Base / Perpendicular

Hypotenuse = √(Base² + Perpendicular²)

sin x = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

cos x = Base / Hypotenuse

**Calculation:**

⇒ Base = 4, Perpendicular = 3

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5

⇒ sin x = 3/5

⇒ cos x = 4/5

Substituting the values into the expression (sin x − cos x) / (sin x + cos x):

⇒ = (3/5 − 4/5) / (3/5 + 4/5)

⇒ = (−1/5) / (7/5)

⇒ = −1/7

**∴ The correct answer is −1/7.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios in a Right Triangle

In any right-angled triangle, sin θ = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse, and tan θ = Perpendicular/Base.

Homogeneous Trigonometric Expressions

If an expression is purely a ratio of terms with the same degree of sin x and cos x, dividing the numerator and denominator by sin x or cos x converts the entire expression into a function of tan x or cot x.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c². The triplet (3, 4, 5) is the most commonly used, and multiples of it like (6, 8, 10) also satisfy the property.

When melting 3D objects to form a new object, the total volume remains conserved.

⇒ Volume of new sphere = Sum of volumes of three small spheres

⇒ (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)πr₁³ + (4/3)πr₂³ + (4/3)πr₃³

⇒ R³ = r₁³ + r₂³ + r₃³

⇒ R³ = 1³ + 6³ + 8³

⇒ R³ = 1 + 216 + 512

⇒ R³ = 729

⇒ R = ³√729 = 9 cm

Now, substitute the value of R into the surface area formula:

⇒ Surface Area of new sphere = 4 × π × (9)²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × 81 × π

⇒ Surface Area = 324π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 324π cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation Principle

When any 3D solid is melted and recast into another shape, the total volume of the material remains constant. Thus, Vᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ = Vfᵢₙₐₗ.

Properties of a Hemisphere

A hemisphere is exactly half of a full sphere. Its Volume is (2/3)πr³, Curved Surface Area is 2πr², and Total Surface Area is 3πr².

Ratio of Attributes of Spheres

If the ratio of the radii of two spheres is a : b, then the ratio of their surface areas will be a² : b², and the ratio of their volumes will be a³ : b³.

questions.question: ABCD is a rhombus in which ∠ADB = 25°. Then, the value of (2 ∠BAD- ∠ABC) is :
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a rhombus, adjacent sides are equal (AD = AB), making ΔABD an isosceles triangle.

⇒ ∠ABD = ∠ADB = 25°

⇒ ∠BAD = 180° − (25° + 25°) = 130°

⇒ ∠ABC = 2 × ∠ABD = 50° (Since the diagonal bisects the angle)

⇒ 2 × ∠BAD − ∠ABC = 2 × 130° − 50° = 210°

**∴ The correct answer is 210°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ABCD is a rhombus.

∠ADB = 25°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c4329ba8393f215d1af70d2ac0c4d0a2f87e2bc0b77ad256843d52f382d7670.png] 

**Calculations:**

In a rhombus, all four sides are of equal length, so AD = AB.

⇒ In ΔABD, sides AD and AB are equal, which means the angles opposite to them are also equal.

⇒ ∠ABD = ∠ADB = 25°

The sum of all interior angles in a triangle is 180°.

⇒ ∠BAD + ∠ABD + ∠ADB = 180°

⇒ ∠BAD + 25° + 25° = 180°

⇒ ∠BAD = 180° − 50° = 130°

We know that the diagonal of a rhombus acts as an angle bisector for the interior angles.

⇒ ∠ABC = 2 × ∠ABD

⇒ ∠ABC = 2 × 25° = 50°

Now, substitute these values into the required expression (2 × ∠BAD − ∠ABC):

⇒ 2 × 130° − 50°

⇒ 260° − 50° = 210°

**∴ The correct answer is 210°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides are of equal length. Opposite angles are equal, and any two adjacent angles are supplementary (their sum is 180°).

Diagonals of a Rhombus

The diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°) and completely bisect the interior angles at the vertices they connect.

Area of a Rhombus

The area can be calculated using the lengths of the diagonals: Area = (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 2, or by using the base and height: Area = Base × Height.
</p

questions.question: A girl cycles from A to B, a distance of 25 km in 2 hours 20 minutes. The road from A is a levelled road for 15 km and then it slopes down to B. The average speed of the girl on the levelled road is 10 km/h. Her average downhill speed (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time = 2 hr 20 min = 7/3 hours

Time spent on levelled road = 15 ÷ 10 = 3/2 hours

Remaining time for downhill = 7/3 − 3/2 = 5/6 hours

Downhill distance = 25 − 15 = 10 km

Downhill speed = 10 ÷ (5/6) = 12 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 25 km

Total time = 2 hours 20 minutes = 2 + 20/60 = 7/3 hours

Distance of levelled road = 15 km

Speed on levelled road = 10 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3270e4b975079e534db4d53ee002e4e4e8e80b5b37a0dcff7ff82e8fb849886c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken to cover the levelled road = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 hours = 3/2 hours

⇒ Remaining distance (downhill) = Total distance − Distance of levelled road

⇒ Remaining distance = 25 − 15 = 10 km

⇒ Remaining time = Total time − Time on levelled road

⇒ Remaining time = 7/3 − 3/2 = (14 − 9) / 6 = 5/6 hours

⇒ Average downhill speed = Remaining distance ÷ Remaining time

⇒ Average downhill speed = 10 ÷ (5/6) = (10 × 6) / 5 = 12 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance covered divided by the total time taken. Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.
</p

questions.question: Amit borrowed a sum of ₹25,000 on simple interest. Bhola borrowed the same amount on compound interest (interest compounded yearly). At the end of 2 years. Bhola had to pay ₹160 more interest than Amit. The rate of interest charged per annum is:

Given R = 30 cm and r = 15 cm. Ratio (r ÷ R) = 1/2.

Diameter of the sphere = 30 cm

When an object is completely submerged in a fluid, it displaces a volume of fluid exactly equal to its own volume regardless of its shape.

questions.question: Sampark Kranti Express left Delhi for Chennai at 14:30 hours, travelling at a speed of 75 km/h, while Rajdhani Express left Delhi for Chennai on the same day at 16:30 hours, travelling at a speed of 90 km/h, travelling on the same route. How far away from Delhi will the two trains meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for meeting distance: D = [S₁ × S₂ × Time Difference] ÷ (S₂ − S₁)

Here, S₁ = 75 km/h, S₂ = 90 km/h, and Time Difference = 16:30 − 14:30 = 2 hours.

D = [75 × 90 × 2] ÷ (90 − 75)

D = 13500 ÷ 15

D = 900 km

**∴ The correct answer is 900 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Sampark Kranti Express = 75 km/h

Departure time of Sampark Kranti = 14:30 hours

Speed of Rajdhani Express = 90 km/h

Departure time of Rajdhani = 16:30 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/533cac8a0b372a20361cb141dc94fe403fdc0c1e9219afb3626028e48260bb13.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time difference between the departures = 16:30 − 14:30 = 2 hours.

⇒ Distance covered by Sampark Kranti Express in these 2 hours = 75 × 2 = 150 km.

⇒ This 150 km is the head start distance between the two trains.

⇒ Relative speed of Rajdhani Express with respect to Sampark Kranti = 90 − 75 = 15 km/h.

⇒ Time taken by Rajdhani Express to catch up = Distance ÷ Relative speed.

⇒ Catch up time = 150 ÷ 15 = 10 hours.

⇒ The meeting distance from Delhi = Speed of Rajdhani × Time taken.

⇒ Distance = 90 × 10 = 900 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 900 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). When they move in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Catch-up Time Formula

Time to meet = Head start distance ÷ Relative speed. This determines the duration required for the faster object to overtake the slower one.

Average Speed

When a journey covers two equal halves at different speeds S₁ and S₂, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).
</p

questions.question: Vineet buys 2 chairs for Rs. 1500. He sold one at 20% profit and the other at 17.5% loss. On the whole, he receives neither loss nor profit. What was the cost of each chair?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the overall transaction results in 0% profit/loss, the profit amount equals the loss amount.

⇒ 20% of CP₁ = 17.5% of CP₂

⇒ Ratio of CP₁ : CP₂ = 17.5 : 20 = 7 : 8

⇒ CP₁ = (7 ÷ 15) × 1500 = Rs. 700 & CP₂ = (8 ÷ 15) × 1500 = Rs. 800

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 700, Rs. 800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Cost Price of two chairs = Rs. 1500

Profit on first chair = 20%

Loss on second chair = 17.5%

Net profit or loss = 0%

**Formula Used:**

When an overall transaction yields neither profit nor loss, the absolute profit earned on one item is exactly equal to the loss incurred on the other item.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a18f2637b90a9f6241599b915aa4e2d6d12b1bf66de7590464c4dd547c3c33f3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the CP of the first chair be x and the second chair be y.

⇒ x + y = 1500

⇒ 20% of x = 17.5% of y

⇒ x ÷ y = 17.5 ÷ 20 = 175 ÷ 200

⇒ x ÷ y = 7 ÷ 8

⇒ Ratio of CP of first chair to second chair = 7 : 8

⇒ Total ratio parts = 7 + 8 = 15

⇒ 15 parts = 1500 ⇒ 1 part = 100

⇒ CP of first chair = 7 × 100 = Rs. 700

⇒ CP of second chair = 8 × 100 = Rs. 800

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 700, Rs. 800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

No Profit No Loss Condition

When a transaction results in no profit and no loss overall, the absolute profit earned on one item is exactly equal to the absolute loss on the other item.

Alligation Cross Method

Used for finding the ratio of base values (like Cost Price) when individual percentages and overall average percentage are given. CP Ratio = (Net % − Loss %) : (Profit % − Net %).

Base of Profit and Loss

Both profit percentage and loss percentage are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise. Profit = SP − CP and Loss = CP − SP.
</p

questions.question: There are 12 men on a Basketball team and in a game 5 of them play at any one time. If the game is 1 hour long and if each man plays exactly the same amount of time, how many minutes does each man play?

Total active playing time on the court = Number of active players × Game duration.

Total playing time = 5 × 60 = 300 minutes.

Time per player = 300 ÷ 12 = 25 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Number of players active on the court at any one time = 5

Duration of the game = 1 hour = 60 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Total player-minutes = Number of active players × Game duration

Time per player = Total player-minutes ÷ Total number of players

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2cd43882848c675448b699fe33db8473cf8fccbb4ed306e6895cbbcf94eee91e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total player-minutes = 5 × 60

Man-Hours Concept

When an activity requires a constant number of individuals active at all times, the total accumulated effort is the product of the active individuals and the duration: Total Time = Active Members × Duration.

questions.question: A can make a divider in 20 days, while B can make it in 50 days. If they work together and get Rs.3500, then find the share of B in the amount.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total work done. If multiple people work together for the exact same duration, their total wages are directly divided in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Efficiency vs Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If the ratio of time taken by A and B to complete a piece of work is a : b, then the ratio of their individual efficiencies will be b : a.

Concepts of time and work apply identically to pipes and cisterns problems. The only key difference is that an outlet or emptying pipe is assigned a negative efficiency.

questions.question: The average speed of a train is 180% of the average speed of a car. The car covers a distance of 990 km in 15 hours. The time taken (in hours) by the train to cover the distance of 891 km is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Speed of the car = 990 ÷ 15 = 66 km/h.

Speed of the train = 180% of 66 = 1.8 × 66 = 118.8 km/h.

Time taken by train = Distance ÷ Speed = 891 ÷ 118.8 = 7.5 hours.

7.5 hours is equal to 7½ hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 7½ hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance covered by car = 990 km

Time taken by car = 15 hours

Average speed of train = 180% of average speed of car

Distance to be covered by train = 891 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/997a032947ac6296bc625af177cb2339ba94cdd8a414c754a66448bf399ad6a5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of the car = 990 ÷ 15

⇒ Speed of the car = 66 km/h

⇒ Speed of the train = 180% of 66

⇒ Speed of the train = (180 ÷ 100) × 66 = 1.8 × 66 = 118.8 km/h

⇒ Time taken by the train = 891 ÷ 118.8

⇒ Time taken by the train = 8910 ÷ 1188

⇒ Time taken by the train = 7.5 hours

⇒ 7.5 hours = 7½ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 7½ hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). In opposite directions, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).

Conversion of Units

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

questions.question: John sold a watch to Sue at a gain of 20%, and Sue sold it to Rima at a profit of 10%. If Rima paid Rs. 2,178 for it, how much did John pay (in Rs.) for the watch?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the multiplying factor method for successive profits:

20% profit = +1/5 ⇒ Multiplier = 6/5

10% profit = +1/10 ⇒ Multiplier = 11/10

Initial Price × (6/5) × (11/10) = Final Price

CP × 66/50 = 2178 ⇒ CP = 2178 × 50/66 = 1650

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1650.**

**Given:**

Profit% earned by John = 20%

Profit% earned by Sue = 10%

Amount paid by Rima = ₹2178

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d6c499fca68e0d9e493e3f1d8ce0f5d7cb4fa30acc66542747b626a36dcc343.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Selling price of John = Cost price of Sue = x × (100 + 20)/100 = 1.2x

⇒ As Rima paid ₹2178, we can equate the values:

⇒ 1.32x = 2178

⇒ x = 2178 ÷ 1.32 = 217800 ÷ 132

⇒ x = 1650

Successive Profit/Loss Formula

Multiplying factors streamline successive changes. A 20% gain gives a multiplier of 1.2, and a 10% gain gives 1.1. Combined multiplier = 1.2 × 1.1 = 1.32.

questions.question: A completes one-third of the work in 5 days. He is then assisted by B. and they together finish the remaining work in 6 days. B alone can complete the entire piece of work in _________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time to complete full work: A = 5 × 3 = 15 days, (A + B) = 6 × (3/2) = 9 days.

Total work = LCM(15, 9) = 45 units.

Efficiency: A = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 units/day, (A + B) = 45 ÷ 9 = 5 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 5 − 3 = 2 units/day.

Time taken by B alone = 45 ÷ 2 = 22.5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.5 days.**

**Given:**

⇒ A completes 1/3 of the work in 5 days.

⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3.

⇒ A and B together complete the remaining 2/3 of the work in 6 days.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by A alone for the whole work = 5 × 3 = 15 days.

⇒ Time taken by (A + B) together for the whole work = 6 × (3/2) = 9 days.

⇒ Let the total work be the LCM of 15 and 9.

⇒ Efficiency of B = 5 − 3 = 2 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 45 ÷ 2 = 22.5 days.
